title: Codex Pets: What They Are and How to Hatch Your Own - Hongkiat
description: Codex Pets are animated desktop companions for OpenAI's Codex app. Here's what they show, why they help, and how to hatch your own.
text: Codex Pets: What They Are and How to Hatch Your Own By Hongkiat.com . in Coding . Updated on May 10, 2026 . Codex now has desktop pets . Yes, really. They are optional animated companions for the Codex app: small floating overlays that sit on your screen while Codex works. The silly part is obvious. The useful part takes about five minutes to notice. A Codex Pet can show whether Codex is running, waiting for input, or ready for review without making you switch back to the app every few minutes. If you already compare coding agents like Codex and Claude Code , this is the softer side of the same product question: how much does the tool help you stay in flow? What Is a Codex Pet? Codex Pets are animated companions built into the Codex app. You can turn one on from Settings > Appearance > Pets , type /pet in the composer, or use the command menu with Cmd + K on Mac or Ctrl + K on Windows. Once active, the pet floats over your desktop and follows the state of the current Codex thread. OpenAI says the overlay can show the active thread, reflect whether Codex is running, waiting for input, or ready for review, and pair that state with a short progress prompt. That means you can leave Codex visible in a small, ambient way while you do something else. How to Turn On a Built-In Pet If your Codex app supports Pets, the fastest way is to type this in the composer: /pet You can also open Settings > Appearance > Pets and choose from the built-in pets there. The same area lets you wake the pet, tuck it away, or refresh custom pets from your local Codex home. If you prefer the keyboard route, open the command menu: Mac: Cmd + K Windows: Ctrl + K Then search for the pet commands. How to Hatch a Custom Codex Pet You are not limited to the built-in pets. OpenAI also has a hatch-pet skill for creating a custom animated pet from a text concept, reference image, or both. First, install the skill from inside Codex: $skill-installer hatch-pet Then reload skills. Open the command menu with Cmd + K or Ctrl + K , choose Force Reload Skills , and ask the skill to create a pet. For example: $hatch-pet create a tiny desk goblin Or: $hatch-pet turn my dog into a Codex pet Or something looser: $hatch-pet create a new pet inspired by my recent projects The skill handles the pet-specific work: concept planning, animation rows, sprite sheet assembly, validation, previews, and packaging. The result is a Codex-compatible pet saved locally, which you can refresh and select from the Pets settings. If you do not know what to hatch, Codex Pets is a small community gallery that can give you ideas for pet styles, themes, and prompts before you make your own. What Makes a Good Pet Prompt? Keep it simple. These pets are small, so clear silhouettes beat elaborate designs. Good prompt ideas: a sleepy raccoon with a tiny laptop a calm duck that looks focused while Codex runs a blue-screen gremlin for debugging sessions a tiny robot with one glowing eye my dog as a pixel-style coding companion Avoid asking for too many props, tiny labels, complex backgrounds, or realistic detail. A Codex Pet needs to read well as a small animated sprite, not as poster art. If you use a reference image, describe what should carry over: color, shape, expression, accessory, or personality. Do not assume the skill will preserve every detail from a photo. Why This Feature Works Codex Pets sound like a joke until you treat them as ambient UI. A coding agent spends a lot of time in states that are easy to miss: still working, waiting for permission, ready for review, stuck on input. A normal app badge or notification can tell you some of that, but a floating overlay keeps the state in your peripheral vision. That is why the feature lands better than it should. It makes Codex feel present without requiring another panel, dashboard, or notification stream. If you want the broader OpenAI tools view, this older roundup of useful ChatGPT tools is a decent snapshot of how quickly the ecosystem keeps shifting. Should You Try It? If you use the Codex app, yes. Turn on a built-in pet first and see whether the overlay helps or annoys you. If it helps, install hatch-pet and make something that fits your workspace. It will not write better code for you. It will not replace good review habits. But it can make long Codex sessions easier to track, and it gives the app a little more personality without getting in the way.
